Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Investing in South Carolina communities

South Carolina’s Community Development Block Grant Program provides funding to eligible towns, cities and counties that do not receive CDBG funds directly from the US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). Grants support projects that strengthen communities, improve infrastructure, expand economic opportunity and address critical local needs.

How to apply Documents & resources
Program guidance

South Carolina's CDBG Program

Administered by SC Commerce’s Business Incentives and Community Development division, the State CDBG Program helps eligible local governments address community needs and create measurable improvements for residents.

Funding is awarded through competitive community development programs, regional planning initiatives and economic development activities. Projects must meet federal and state requirements, respond to an identified community need and align with South Carolina’s Consolidated Plan for Housing and Community Development.

Programs & application guidelines

Programs and funding categories are established at the beginning of each program year. Current program documents explain eligible project types, application requirements, funding categories and other conditions applicants must meet.

Review the following materials before requesting an application:

2026 Annual Action Plan 2026 CDBG Program Description 2026 CDBG Application Guidelines
Eligibility

Eligibility

Who can apply?

Only units of general local government, including eligible towns, cities and counties, may apply for State CDBG funding.

Some jurisdictions receive annual CDBG allocations directly from HUD and are not eligible to apply through the State CDBG Program. Current entitlement jurisdictions include:

  • Berkeley, Charleston, Greenville, Horry, Lexington, Richland and Spartanburg counties
  • Municipalities of Aiken, Anderson, Charleston, Columbia, Florence, Greenville, Hilton Head Island, Rock Hill, Spartanburg, Summerville and Sumter
  • Municipalities participating in an entitlement county’s urban county designation

All other South Carolina municipalities and counties may be eligible to apply. Consult the current CDBG Program Description to confirm eligibility.

What can CDBG support?

Eligible projects may include:

  • Water, sewer, road and drainage improvements
  • Public facilities and equipment
  • Downtown and neighborhood revitalization
  • Streetscape and sidewalk improvements
  • Clearance and demolition activities
  • Economic development infrastructure
  • Job creation and retention initiatives
  • Community and regional planning activities

Every proposed project must involve an activity permitted under federal law, meet the requirements of the applicable funding category and satisfy a CDBG national objective.

National objectives

National objectives

Every project funded through the State CDBG Program must meet at least one of three national objectives.

Benefit low- and moderate-income persons

Projects may qualify by providing an area benefit, serving a limited clientele, supporting eligible housing activities or creating or retaining jobs for low- and moderate-income residents.

Elimination or prevention of slums and blight

Projects may qualify by addressing conditions that contribute to deterioration, blight or threats to the health and safety of a community.

Urgent need

Use of the urgent need objective is extremely rare and is reserved for activities that alleviate emergency conditions. To qualify:

  • Existing conditions must pose a serious and immediate threat to the health or welfare of the community
  • The conditions must be of recent origin or have recently become urgent, generally within the previous 18 months
  • The applicant must be unable to finance the activity independently
  • Other sources of funding must be unavailable

Program LMI benefit requirement

Federal regulations require the State CDBG Program to expend at least 70% of its funds on activities benefiting low- and moderate-income persons. South Carolina therefore prioritizes projects that qualify under this national objective.

Projects qualifying under the slums and blight or urgent need objectives do not contribute toward the program’s overall LMI benefit requirement and are funded more selectively.

Public notices

Public notices & hearings

Public participation helps shape South Carolina’s community development priorities and plans for the use of federal funding.

2026-2030 Consolidated Plan

The 2026-2030 Consolidated Plan includes the 2026 Annual Action Plan and the 2026 CDBG Program Description. The plan was available for public review from January 18 through February 19, 2026.

A public hearing was held January 28, 2026, to discuss the Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan.

Publicly owned land database

Section 104 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (Public Law 119-101) requires Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) grantees to maintain a publicly accessible, searchable database of undeveloped land they own.

Disaster recovery & mitigation

The regular State CDBG Program is administered by SC Commerce. Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery and Mitigation programs in South Carolina are administered by the South Carolina Office of Resilience.

Visit SCOR for information about disaster recovery programs, mitigation resources, eligibility requirements and available assistance.
